what_students_are_told: Help choosing the right modules, changing your curriculum, and making a plan if you fall behind.
A senior student mentor who helps you settle in, find your way around and cope with the first semester.
Food parcels, vouchers or meals for students who are struggling to afford food.
The financial aid office and the SRC help follow up on late or missing allowances, appeals and other funding problems.

what_it_is: Check a room before you pay
what_students_are_told: Use the list of accredited off-campus accommodation. View the room in person, get a written lease, and confirm an agent's registration with the PPRA. Search the photos online, and never pay a deposit under pressure.
Every residence has a house committee and peer mentors who can help with noise, roommates, study space and settling in.
Study spaces that stay open after lectures, and student communities for those who don't live on campus.
Prescribed textbooks are kept on short-loan
column4: so you can use them without buying.

what_students_are_told: There's no single right answer. Decide upfront what share of your money you can send each month, put it in your budget, and tell home when your money arrives so they can plan too.
One-on-one help to plan your study time, prepare for tests and manage clashing deadlines.
Free, confidential counselling, in person or online. You don't need to be in crisis to go.
Key modules unlock second-year modules, and funders check how many credits you pass.
Teams, cultural, faith, academic and hobby societies: a cheap way to meet people and feel at home.

what_it_is: How monthly debit orders add up
what_students_are_told: Gym contracts, phone contracts and subscriptions all leave your account automatically. Add up every debit order before signing, and check the cancellation terms.

what_it_is: Computer labs, Wi-Fi and device support
what_students_are_told: Open computer labs, library computers and free campus Wi-Fi, plus laptop loans and device support for students who need them.
Campus tours, welcome events and first-year sessions on where to find help.
Residence waiting lists, temporary placements and the list of accredited private accommodation.
Payment arrangements, fee statements, and information on programmes that help with historic student debt.
CV help, mock interviews, career fairs where employers come to campus, vacation work and graduate programme advice, and help if you're unsure about your course.
Your lecturers set aside hours every week for students. Few students use them, and they make a real difference.
Free or low-cost, confidential health care: illness, contraception, pregnancy tests and sexual health.
Free, confidential support for students, 24 hours a day, including mental health and gender-based violence.
Campus security, marked safe walking routes (green routes), and escorts or shuttles between campus and residences after dark.
Support and a confidential way to report discrimination, harassment or unfair treatment.
Help with settling in, study permits and peer groups for students from other countries.
Free workshops and one-on-one sessions on time management, academic writing, study methods and exam preparation, run by the academic development unit and the writing centre.
Applications are made on each university's own official website, and they open and close on different dates. Fill it in yourself, and keep your reference number and every confirmation email.

NSFAS applications are free and are made only on the official NSFAS website. Bursaries come from universities, companies, foundations and government departments, and each has its own requirements and closing date.

Nobody can sell you a place or guaranteed funding. Don't let a stranger apply for you, and never share your ID number, passwords or one-time PINs. Application and NSFAS help is free at your school and at the university.
Residences provide a bed, a desk and a cupboard, but not bedding, a lock, crockery or cleaning things. Private rooms vary: some are furnished and some are empty.
Your student card opens the library, computer labs, residences and test venues, so get it in your first days. Queues are longest in registration week.
A supplementary exam is a second chance to write a module you narrowly failed. The result codes on your portal say whether you passed, failed or were admitted to one.
